# Draft:Monument of Queen Marie from Chișinău

| designer     = Veaceslav Jiglițchi (sculptor); Mihail Andrieș (architect)
| material     = Bronze; Cosăuți stone
| height       = 6 m (total); statue 3.8 m; pedestal 2.2 m
| complete     = 27 March 2025
| open         = 27 March 2025
| dedicated_to = Maria Alexandra Victoria of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha
}}
The Statue of Queen Maria of Romania in Chișinău is a bronze monument made by Moldovan sculptor Veaceslav Jiglițchi (b. 6 February 1970, Slobozia village, Ștefan Vodă district) and dedicated to the second Queen of Romania, Maria Alexandra Victoria of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha (1875–1938).
The statue is located in the square of one of the oldest institutions in Bessarabia, the Zemstvo Girls' Lyceum No. 1, which bore her name between 1918 and 1940. Today the building houses the Romanian–French Theoretical Lyceum "Gheorghe Asachi".
The statue was erected following Government Decision No. 153/2022 [https://old.cancelaria.gov.md/sites/default/files/document/attachments/proiect-nu_19_mc_2022.pdf] regarding the establishment in Chișinău of the monument "Maria Alexandra Victoria of Saxe – Cotha, Queen of Romania". The author of the monument was selected through a competition organised by the civic association "Monumentum", and the project was approved by the Ministry of Culture.
History
Initiatives
The idea to erect a monument in Chișinău in honour of Queen Maria dates back to 1939, as recognition of her role in the realisation and consolidation of Greater Romania, including the unification of Bessarabia with Romania, but the project was abandoned after the geopolitical changes of 1940 and the annexation of Bessarabia by the USSR.
The initiative was revived in 2018 and resumed by lawyer Iulian Rusanovschi on the occasion of the Centenary of the Great Union. Funds were raised by public subscription through the non-governmental association "Monumentum".
Sculpting took place in the workshop of Veaceslav Jiglițchi in Chișinău, while the Cosăuți stone pedestal was worked in workshops at Cosăuți in 2021.
Inauguration
The statue was inaugurated on 27 March 2025, in the square of the Romanian–French Lyceum "Gheorghe Asachi", as part of commemorations of the 107th anniversary of the Union of Bessarabia with Romania.
The inauguration was organised by A.O. "Monumentum" together with an initiative group (Iulian Rusanovschi, Mihail Andrieș, Sergiu Covali, Ion Deli) and attended by officials including the rector of Moldova State University Igor Șarov and academician Grigore Tincă. The ceremony included performances by the Border Police brass band and the national anthems of the Republic of Moldova and Romania.‘Your Majesty, welcome back to Chișinău.’With this message, the monument was inaugurated.
Description of the monument
The Statue of Queen Maria is represented supernatural, being placed on a pedestal of stone from Cosăuți, having a height of 6m. The project was elaborated by the architect Mihail Andrieș. The Queen is depicted on the day of her coronation at Alba Iulia 15 October 1922, holding in her left hand the Christian Bible. The statue is made of bronze and has a height of 3.8m, and the pedestal was worked by the folk stonemason Marin Lozan and has 2.2m. The monument was cast in Chișinău by SJ&B STUDIO. On each face of the pedestal, the visual artist conceived and realised an ornamental bas-relief in bronze, representing narrative scenes with symbolic and memorial function from the life of Queen Maria.
Description of the images
*
The first plaque, on the right side, illustrates a scene from the coronation day on 15 October 1922, at Alba Iulia, an event with major historical and symbolic significance, in which Queen Maria is represented alongside King Ferdinand as sovereigns of Greater Romania.
*
The second plaque, on the left side, represents the Queen's involvement during the First World War. Queen Maria organised field hospitals and, dressed in the clothing of a nursing sister, was present at the front, distributing medicines, food and blankets to the wounded soldiers at the front or to those ill with typhus. The image of the Queen in the Red Cross uniform remained in the memory of those who knew her.
Queen Maria dedicated herself to the Romanian people, and procuring medicines, direct involvement in caring for the sick and the wounded, had become an essential part of her life. Queen Maria was loved by Romanians, being nicknamed "the mother of the wounded" and "the Soldier Queen".
Inscription on the memorial plaque
"THE INITIATIVE TO ERECT THE STATUE OF QUEEN MARIA IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF CHIȘINĂU WAS LAUNCHED BY LAWYER IULIAN RUSANOVECHI, ON 27 MARCH 2018, IN THE CONTEXT OF THE CELEBRATION OF THE CENTENARY OF THE UNION OF BASARABIA WITH ROMANIA AND THE FORMATION OF THE MODERN ROMANIAN STATE. MAJOR ACHIEVEMENTS ACCOMPLISHED DURING THE REIGN OF KING FERDINAND I AND QUEEN MARIA. IN THIS WAY THE IDEA PROMOTED IN 1939 TO EVOKE THE PERSONALITY OF QUEEN MARIA BY ERECTING AN EMBLEMATIC MONUMENT IN CHIȘINĂU WAS REACTUALIZED..."
Postcard
On 27 March 2025, the state postal enterprise Poșta Moldovei issued a commemorative postcard and a special postmark for the inauguration of the monument.
